messages.author: 9160793b546521df
messages.subject: BYM with fine grid
parts:
Hey everyone, 

I am playing with R-INLA and have the following code:

# convert adjacency matrix into an INLA format
W.nb1km <- poly2nb(dry.grid1km)

nb2INLA("W.adj1km", W.nb1km)

dry.grid1km$ID <- 1:nrow(dry.grid1km@data)

data_temp <- dry.grid1km@data[,c("ncase", "offset")]
data_temp$str <- 1:nrow(data_temp)
data_temp$intercept <- 1

formula <- ncase ~ -1 + intercept + f(str, model="bym", graph="W.adj1km", constr=TRUE,  scale.model=TRUE, hyper = list(prec.unstruct = list(
  prior = "gaussian", param=c(0,1)), prec.spatial = list(prior="gaussian", param=c(0,1))))


Model_INLA_1km <- inla(formula, family="poisson", data=as.data.frame(data_temp), control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
                       E = data_temp$offset, control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE), verbose = TRUE)

I perfomed the above code for 10, 5 and 3 km grid but it crashes every time I try 1km grid. I thought it might be due to the great amount of 0s on the outcome and thus I also tried poisson zero-inflated but it still crashes. Any ideas?

Thanx in advance, 
Akis

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] BYM with fine grid
parts:
How many cells are in a 1km grid? You may have hit a memory issue. 

Can you rerun with verbose=TRUE and send the output?

Thanks

Dan
